question: Which main chemical in tobacco makes it so addictive?
explanation: Nicotine is the addictive substance in tobacco that hooks the brain and drives the urge to keep smoking. You've got this! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why do regular smokers need to smoke more over time to feel the same buzz?

options.A: Their lungs have expanded and require more volume
options.B: Their social circles encourage heavier smoking habits
options.C: Their brains have developed tolerance to the chemical
options.D: The tobacco companies put weaker ingredients in newer packs

explanation: Tolerance happens when the brain gets so used to nicotine that it needs higher amounts to feel that same initial effect. Great job thinking this through! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is a common tobacco trend among young people in Nigerian cities today?

options.A: A total shift toward chewing raw tobacco leaves exclusively
options.B: A complete halt in all forms of smoking
options.C: The rising popularity of manufactured cigarettes and shisha
options.D: The replacement of tobacco with herbal medicinal teas

explanation: Smart marketing has made manufactured cigarettes and waterpipes (shisha) very popular among urban youth. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h2)

question: How does widespread tobacco use create a double challenge for Nigeria's health system?

options.A: It reduces the overall population so much that clinics have no patients to treat
options.B: It causes nurses to leave public clinics for international job opportunities
options.C: It forces hospitals to buy expensive imported equipment for infectious diseases only
options.D: It requires managing rising lifestyle diseases alongside existing infectious disease challenges

explanation: Clinics have to juggle treating traditional infectious diseases while also handling a growing wave of chronic illnesses caused by tobacco. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which tiny, hair-like parts of the respiratory tract get paralyzed and destroyed by cigarette smoke?
explanation: Cilia are the tiny sweeping brushes of the lungs that clear out mucus and dirt. Smoke damages them badly, but understanding this puts you one step ahead! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h3)

question: A 30-year smoker comes in with severe breathlessness and a chronic cough. Which condition affecting the tiny air sacs is most likely the cause?
explanation: Long-term smoking destroys the delicate walls of the alveoli (air sacs), leading to emphysema and trapped air. You're building solid clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why do people trying to quit smoking often get sudden cravings when doing routine things, like drinking morning tea?

options.A: Their physical lungs are suddenly damaged by the beverage steam
options.B: The brain has formed strong behavioral links between those routines and smoking
options.C: Their immune system is reacting to dietary changes
options.D: The tea contains hidden traces of chemical nicotine

explanation: Daily habits act as triggers because the brain links those routines directly to smoking. Recognizing this helps us support patients better! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h4)

question: Even after physical withdrawal fades, why is quitting smoking still so tough?

options.A: Commercial cigarettes contain permanent cellular dyes
options.B: Social laws make it illegal to stop smoking abruptly
options.C: The body continues producing natural nicotine forever
options.D: Psychological habits and environmental triggers remain deeply ingrained

explanation: The mental habit and social triggers stick around long after the physical chemicals leave the body. Don't worry if this takes time to master! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h4)

question: In the '5 As' smoking cessation framework, which step means checking if a patient uses tobacco during every clinic visit?
explanation: The 'Ask' step is simply checking and recording whether every patient uses tobacco. Simple, direct, and essential for good nursing care! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h5)

question: During community outreach, a nurse asks a client if they are ready to stop smoking today. Which of the '5 As' is this?
explanation: Checking a patient's willingness and readiness to quit falls right under the 'Assess' step. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which of the '5 Rs' motivational counseling steps helps a patient spot personal barriers and challenges to quitting?
explanation: Looking at 'Roadblocks' helps patients plan for tough things like stress, urges, and social pressure. You've got a great grasp of patient communication! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h6)

question: A patient says quitting is pointless because their health is already ruined. Which 'R' should the nurse use first to motivate them?
explanation: Connecting quitting directly to their personal health situation makes the conversation meaningful to them. Excellent clinical reasoning! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of using Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT) when trying to quit?

options.A: It delivers controlled nicotine doses without toxic tar and carbon monoxide
options.B: It permanently repairs lung tissue damage overnight
options.C: It numbs the throat so the patient can never taste tobacco again

explanation: NRT gives clean nicotine to ease withdrawal without exposing the body to the dangerous toxins found in cigarette smoke. Brilliant work! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why do experts recommend combining medication with behavioral counseling instead of using medication alone?

options.A: Counseling addresses the psychological habits while medication treats physical cravings
options.B: Government health insurance policies forbid giving out prescriptions alone
options.C: Medications are too expensive for patients to buy without counseling
options.D: Medications only work if the patient attends weekly support group meetings

explanation: Tackling both the physical craving and the mental habit gives the patient the absolute best chance at success. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which public health policy is proven to stop young people from starting to smoke?

options.A: Lowering the age restriction for purchasing cigars
options.B: Allowing tobacco companies to sponsor school sports
options.C: Providing free ashtrays in public parks

explanation: Higher taxes raise cigarette prices, making them much harder for price-sensitive teens to afford. Every public health measure counts! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h8)

question: What is the main goal of community nursing advocacy for smoke-free indoor public spaces?

options.A: To protect non-smokers and children from the dangers of secondhand smoke
options.B: To help current smokers reduce their daily cigarette count
options.C: To reduce the government spending on imported medical supplies
options.D: To eliminate all tobacco farming in rural agricultural areas

explanation: Smoke-free rules ensure that people who don't smoke aren't forced to breathe in harmful tobacco smoke. Amazing job completing this session! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h8)
